summary: Prasarn Lao-areun is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He earned a PhD from the University of Mysore (attested 2014) and studied under Viroj Inthanon.

Pratap Kumar Penumala (born 1952) specializes in religious studies and Indology. His career includes posts as Professor at the University of KwaZulu-Natal (attested 2010) and Visiting Professor at Colorado College (attested 2010).

Pratapaditya Pal (born 1935) works in Indology, Tibetology, and history and archaeology. He held posts at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art (~1970–1995, attested 2007) and the Art Institute of Chicago in 1995.
Prayoon Mererk (born 1955) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Delhi by 1985, supervised by Margaret Chatterjee and Mahesh Tiwary.

Prods Oktor Skjærvø (born 1944) studied at the University of Oslo (PhD 1981) and University of Mainz (Dr. habil. 1984). In Iranian studies and linguistics, he held posts at Mainz, Columbia University, and Harvard University (~1991–2014).

Projit Bihari Mukharji studied at Presidency University, JNU, and SOAS. A specialist in Indology and history and archaeology, he has held posts at Newcastle University, McMaster University, the University of Pennsylvania, and Ashoka University.
Pulinbihari Chakravarti worked in Indology and philosophy, studying under Jogendranath Vedantatirtha and Satkari Mookerjee. He served as Curator of Manuscripts at the Asiatic Society (attested 1951).

Purushottama Bilimoria, who studied under Shivesh Thakur and earned a PhD at La Trobe University, works in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He held posts at Deakin University, University of Melbourne, Stony Brook, Columbia, and UC Berkeley.
Pyi Phyo Kyaw is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from King's College London by 2014 and later served there as a postdoctoral research fellow (attested 2017).
Pál Miklós (1927–2002) was a scholar of sinology and history and archaeology. He completed studies at Eötvös Loránd University (~1946–1950) and Peking University (~1950–1954).

Péter-Dániel Szántó, working in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, studied at Eötvös Loránd University and Balliol College under Alexis Sanderson. He has held posts at All Souls College, the University of Oxford, and Eötvös Loránd University.

Qian Lin works in Buddhist studies. She studied at Fudan University, the University of Bristol, and the University of Washington (PhD 2015), supervised by Collett Cox and taught by Rupert Gethin among others.

Qiang Ning is a scholar of history and archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology who studied under Wu Hung and Irene Winter. He has held teaching posts at Michigan, Yale, and San Diego State, and was a researcher at Dunhuang Academy.

Qichao Liang (1873–1929) worked in sinology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He studied under Kang Youwei (~1890–1892) and at National Tsing Hua University, later holding a post at Tsinghua University (~1925–1929).

Qing Duan (1953–2022) specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She studied at Peking University and the University of Hamburg, later serving as Professor at Peking University (~1998–2022).

Qingying Chen (1942–2022) studied at Qinghai Normal University, Qinghai University for Nationalities, and Minzu University of China. Working in Tibetology and history, he held posts at Minzu University, Southwest Minzu University, and China Tibetology Research Center (~1986–2012).
Qingzhi Zhu works in linguistics, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He has held professorial posts at Peking University (attested 2004) and The Education University of Hong Kong (attested 2010).
Qinni Liu is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Jurievitch Solonin (attested 2009).
Qiwen Xiao is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2013).
R. Balasubramanian (1929–2017) was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied under Varahur Kalyanasundara Sastri. He served as Director at the University of Madras (~1975–1990).
